attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis. The surgical pathology showed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and positive surgical margins. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 12 and the difference between the biopsy grade (Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1) and the prostatectomy specimen grade (Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2). The nodal status was negative, as nodes were sampled and no metastasis was found.

Information that would revise this prognosis significantly would be the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. A documented postoperative PSA level and its trend would be crucial for assessing recurrence risk. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 58.9 months without an event. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data widens the uncertainty regarding future disease control.

The patient underwent robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage pT2, Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion or lymph node metastasis. The biopsy demonstrated a Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1) pattern. These findings, particularly the positive margins and higher Gleason grade, are factors driving the prognosis. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis and the absence of lymphovascular invasion. The preoperative PSA was 12.

The prognosis is estimated with a numeric horizon of 58.9 months without an event. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data would revise this prognosis and its subsequent trajectory. Nodal status was documented as negative, which reduces uncertainty regarding nodal involvement. The discrepancy between the biopsy grade (Group 1) and the prostatectomy grade (Group 2) is a point of note.
